In the first hour you'll learn about Methylene Blue, liver, gallbladder, and heavy metals detox, magnesium, vitamin B, C and K2, reversing tooth decay, getting chlorine and fluoride out of your water, sodium bicarbonate, and more.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension, Clive shares personal out of body experiences, getting the cow-poke out of people's systems, the potential next round of cooties paranoia, carbon and charcoal, cryotherapy and other experimental treatments, hydrogen, allergies solutions, and communicating with our body's innate intelligence.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Leaving the Body, With and Without Help", "body": "The extension opens on out of body experiences, and both men bring stories. Clive recalls fishing in the Caribbean at 11, catching nothing while the fish seemed to read his reluctance and give themselves to his companion. At 15 he raided his school's chemistry store, found ether, and floated on the ceiling above his own body, disappointed to return. He describes ketamine as a dissociative anesthetic rather than a party drug. Chance shares leaving his body on the last day of a colon cleanse, drifting to the ceiling fan fully conscious, and an apparent bilocation at a music festival."}, {"title": "One Primary Sense and a Chosen Life", "body": "Chance proposes that the senses are not separate inputs racing to the brain but divisions of one primary energetic connection to reality, with synesthesia as that division working differently. Clive answers with experiments in which subjects' brains reacted to frightening images before a random number generator had even produced them, suggesting more than one kind of time. From there the talk turns to oneness: Clive sees us as the one split into many to experience everything, and Chance adds that each person is a portal the divine views itself through. Asked whether he chose to be here, Chance calls that belief the way out of victimhood."}, {"title": "Terrain Thinking and the Question of Diagnosis", "body": "Returning to health, Clive offers his own views on detoxing after the recent injections and on what he sees as the strategy behind a coming new variant, framing both as opinion. Chance then raises germ theory versus terrain theory, saying the truth usually sits in between. Clive places himself firmly on the terrain side, pointing to friends who fell ill only once their holidays began and reading colds and flus as the body choosing a restful moment to clear itself out. He adds his own definition, that diagnosis means two people not knowing, while Chance prefers calling the system health scare rather than healthcare."}, {"title": "Carbon, Cold and a Cutting Edge Clinic", "body": "Chance asks about biochar, pyrolyzed carbon made by his friend Christopher Gardner, host of BioCharisma. Clive, whose friend runs England's biggest biochar producer, had only heard of it for soil, and explains that charcoal adsorbs toxins rather than absorbing them, favoring natural charcoal from deep-rooted hardwoods. He then describes scouting treatments for a possible clinic: the Vasper bike with cooled compression cuffs, a cryo chamber at minus 110 Celsius, an ex-NASA artificial sun, EE Systems, where he personally felt nothing, and blood filtering in Germany, where some people's extracted bags showed layers a doctor called microplastics and bacteria, and which left Clive tired for weeks."}, {"title": "Hydrogen, Allergies and the Body That Knows", "body": "Chance credits a gifted Aquacure with faster workout recovery, and Clive muses that pH means potential hydrogen and that bodies full of hydrogen and magnesium are remarkably explosive. On allergies, Chance traces his own path through a vegan stretch and the later return of cleaner dairy, reading allergies as repressed irritation. Clive breaks dairy into the animal's feed and older breeds like Jerseys and Guernseys, and describes a calm pulse test for any food. Both prize asking the body directly: Clive through kinesiology techniques that halve boxes of supplements, Chance through ear pops during tuning, plus a heart to heart hug that seems to change arm strength."}]
